name: Board and HIL
description: For firmware on a real board: a researcher works out the board, a rig engineer sets up flashing and on-board tests before the build, and a firmware reviewer checks the result against the hardware.

start.name: Board researcher
start.purpose: Works out what is on the board and how it is wired, from the files you gave or from the internet when you only named the board.
reads: the .ioc, schematic, PCB layout and BOM files in this workspace
the board and MCU documentation online
produces: .devcrew/hardware/board.md: MCU, clocks, pin table, external parts, programming and serial interfaces, sources, assumptions and conflicts

start.name: HIL rig engineer
start.purpose: Sets up how the AI can flash the real board, watch its serial output and run tests on it, without two runs using the same board at once.
reads: the build files in this workspace (Makefile, CMakeLists.txt, .ioc)
produces: .devcrew/hil/: rig.json, probe.sh, flash.sh, monitor.sh, run.sh with a per-board lock, and RIG.md with setup steps and the commands tests call

afterBuild.name: Firmware reviewer
afterBuild.purpose: Checks the firmware against the real board and sends it back to Dev if it would misbehave on the hardware.
produces: .devcrew/firmware-review.md: a verdict and hardware-related findings by severity
